title: Philippines, Japan envoys sign notes for emergency loan
summary: The Philippines and Japan signed and exchanged notes for an “Emergency Support Loan” of up to 70 billion yen for “Enhancing Economic Resilience and Poverty Alleviation,” the…

blocks.text: Japanese Ambassador Katsuro Kitagawa and Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro signed the loan program on Nov. 13.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Japan signed and exchanged notes for an “Emergency Support Loan” of up to 70 billion yen for “Enhancing Economic Resilience and Poverty Alleviation,” the Japanese embassy announced yesterday.

With its reliance on the Middle East for approximately 95 percent of its crude oil and petroleum requirements, the Philippines is significantly affected by increasing energy and raw material prices, as well as supply chain instability stemming from the situation in the Middle East sparked by the US attack on Iran.
“Rising production costs and logistical bottlenecks are posing challenges to the stable supply of products that underpin Japan’s supply chains,” the Japanese embassy said in a statement.
